answer:
To find the remainder when the 100th term of the Lucas sequence is divided by 8, we first note that the Lucas sequence is defined by the recurrence relation \( L_n = L_{n-1} + L_{n-2} \) with initial terms \( L_1 = 1 \) and \( L_2 = 3 \). 

We compute the sequence modulo 8 to identify any periodic behavior:

\[
\begin{aligned}
&L_1 \equiv 1 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_2 \equiv 3 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_3 \equiv (1 + 3) \equiv 4 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_4 \equiv (3 + 4) \equiv 7 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_5 \equiv (4 + 7) \equiv 11 \equiv 3 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_6 \equiv (7 + 3) \equiv 10 \equiv 2 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_7 \equiv (3 + 2) \equiv 5 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_8 \equiv (2 + 5) \equiv 7 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_9 \equiv (5 + 7) \equiv 12 \equiv 4 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_{10} \equiv (7 + 4) \equiv 11 \equiv 3 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_{11} \equiv (4 + 3) \equiv 7 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_{12} \equiv (3 + 7) \equiv 10 \equiv 2 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_{13} \equiv (7 + 2) \equiv 9 \equiv 1 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_{14} \equiv (2 + 1) \equiv 3 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_{15} \equiv (1 + 3) \equiv 4 \pmod{8}, \\
&L_{16} \equiv (3 + 4) \equiv 7 \pmod{8}, \\
\end{aligned}
\]

We observe that the sequence modulo 8 repeats every 12 terms starting from \( L_{13} \). Therefore, the Pisano period modulo 8 is 12. 

To find \( L_{100} \mod 8 \), we compute the remainder of 100 divided by 12:
\[
100 \div 12 = 8 \text{ remainder } 4
\]

Thus, \( L_{100} \equiv L_4 \pmod{8} \). From our earlier computation, \( L_4 \equiv 7 \pmod{8} \).

The remainder when the 100th term of the Lucas sequence is divided by 8 is \(\boxed{7}\).
